title: LangGraph checkpoint/resume adapter probe for ZAgenticLoop
summary: The second authenticated fresh research pass supports LangGraph's checkpointer storage contract as a narrow, testable capability, but does not establish complete interrupt/resume identity semantics, a native TypeScript/Node.js seam, or authority over ZAgenticLoop execution. Keep the native core and run one removable adapter probe against the native checkpoint fixture; any authority bypass, identity drift, digest drift, or failed removal is a hard stop.

concepts.value: ZAgenticLoop 的 native checkpoint fixture 与 resume oracle 是 conformance 事实源，固定 execution identity、checkpoint metadata、state digest、duplicate、Evidence、verification、Human acceptance 与 authority。
LangGraph 的 BaseCheckpointSaver conformance surface 关注 blob round-trip、metadata preservation、namespace isolation、incremental updates 等存储语义。
外部 checkpointer 只通过 envelope 进入 native core，不能创建第二 execution authority 或改写 native lifecycle facts。
编译器 mechanical match 不等于语义闭合；thread/interrupt resume identity、Node/TS seam、security/approval ownership 仍需单独验证。
当前只验证一个可丢弃的 durable-state/checkpoint vertical slice，不承担 whole-framework adoption 或 production runtime commitment。

cards.title: langchain-ai/langgraph / checkpointer storage capability
cards.summary: Fresh evidence supports a separately testable BaseCheckpointSaver storage contract and a Postgres persistence implementation for durable workflows. The evidence is sufficient for a bounded storage adapter probe, not for whole-framework or native Node.js adoption.

claims.text: LangGraph's first-party checkpoint conformance suite validates a BaseCheckpointSaver storage contract covering blob round-trips, metadata preservation, namespace isolation, and incremental channel updates.
The first-party Postgres checkpointer is documented as persistence for durable, long-running workflows and agents, with Psycopg 3 as part of its installation boundary.

The conformance package is a separately versioned storage test surface, so it can be treated as a candidate adapter seam rather than evidence that the entire framework must become the host product authority.
The fresh evidence points to a PyPI/API and Psycopg/Python runtime boundary; it does not establish a native TypeScript/Node.js checkpointer seam for the ZAgenticLoop host.

The current fresh excerpts establish durable storage but do not directly establish thread_id, interrupt, Command-resume identity, or duplicate-delivery behavior; these remain unverified before the adapter can continue.

The A34 Architecture Study of the pinned ZAgenticLoop working tree shows that the native checkpoint fixture binds execution identity, state digest, duplicate delivery, Evidence, verification, Human acceptance, and native-core authority; this is the host-side conformance oracle, not a LangGraph capability claim.

A checkpointer storage contract does not establish authority over ZAgenticLoop approvals, credentials, sandbox policy, Evidence provenance, Human acceptance, or lifecycle closeout; those responsibilities remain native and are tested as hard-stop boundaries.

comparisons.text: The native fixture defines the complete semantic oracle, while LangGraph evidence defines a narrower storage contract. The adapter is acceptable only when the external checkpoint maps back to the native execution identity, metadata, digest, and duplicate rules.

Durable Postgres-backed storage is useful evidence for persistence, but durable storage is not the same as proven interrupt/resume identity, duplicate delivery, or recovery semantics. The latter must be tested in the probe.

The Python/PyPI/Psycopg boundary may require a process or service adapter in a TypeScript/Node.js host. Until the runtime seam and ownership are measured, this is an unverified integration cost rather than a reason to adopt the framework core.

Keeping execution, Evidence, verification, Human acceptance, security, and lifecycle native makes the external capability removable. Any adapter path that duplicates those facts creates a second authority and must stop.

recommendations.text: Keep ZAgenticLoop's native Graph/OPN core and do not adopt LangGraph as the execution or lifecycle authority. Use LangGraph only as a candidate checkpointer capability behind a provider-neutral adapter.

Define the adapter envelope around source execution/task/attempt, source revision, checkpoint namespace and id, artifact reference, state digest, and native execution identity. Reject any checkpoint that cannot reconstruct or verify those bindings.

Run one isolated experience-version probe covering checkpoint write/read, namespace, metadata, process restart, interrupt/resume, duplicate delivery, retry, and state digest. The current thread/interrupt behavior is unverified and must be closed with primary evidence or runtime tests before a continue decision.

Treat Node/TypeScript integration, Python/Psycopg process ownership, version skew, credentials, sandbox, and rollback as explicit validation gates. Do not add a runtime dependency until the adapter owner and failure recovery are bounded.

Hard-stop on authority bypass, changed execution identity, second execution authority, Evidence or verification digest drift, Human acceptance bypass, side effects before acceptance, or any native-oracle failure.

After the probe, remove the adapter and rerun the native fixture. Continue only if the native path remains unchanged and all critical scenarios pass; otherwise defer or stop. The unverified Node/TS seam and resume semantics must remain visible in the closeout.

metrics.definition: Native fixture scenarios that the external checkpoint adapter reproduces without semantic drift
metrics.method: Run write/read, metadata, namespace, incremental update, resume, duplicate, retry, and digest cases against native and adapter paths
metrics.condition: Any identity, authority, digest, or acceptance bypass is a hard failure

metrics.definition: Resumed work items that retain the native execution id, task id, attempt, agent id, checkpoint id, and state digest
metrics.method: Inject restart, interrupt, retry, and duplicate delivery, then compare the resume observation with the native oracle
metrics.condition: No second execution authority may be created

metrics.definition: Checkpoint reads that cannot cross the native task/network/namespace boundary
metrics.method: Attempt cross-task, cross-network, stale-revision, and wrong-agent reads
metrics.condition: Every unauthorized read is rejected and auditable

metrics.definition: Resumed Evidence and verification bindings that retain the expected digest and execution identity
metrics.method: Tamper with checkpoint state, artifact refs, Evidence digests, verification digests, and review handoff refs
metrics.condition: Any drift blocks the oracle and prevents side effects

metrics.definition: New runtime, process, package, upgrade, credential, and incident responsibilities introduced by the adapter
metrics.method: Inventory Python/Psycopg or Node bridge processes, version-skew cases, deploy/rollback steps, and owners
metrics.condition: Unowned or unbounded obligations block continuation
metrics.expected: One removable adapter with explicit owner and rollback

metrics.definition: Unverified resume, interrupt, Node/TS, security, and approval criteria closed by primary evidence or reproducible probe results
metrics.method: Track each criterion from the A34 evidence gap list to a pinned source or test artifact
metrics.condition: Unknown is not rewritten as absent; no framework-core decision before closure

metrics.definition: Native fixture and resume oracle scenarios that still pass after deleting the external adapter
metrics.method: Remove adapter package/process/config and rerun the native build and conformance suite
metrics.condition: Native semantic owner must not require the external framework
